entities.summary: Federico Caccia (1684-1699) was a renowned Italian diplomat, Cardinal, and Archbishop of Milan, playing a pivotal role in European politics during the late 17th century. Born in unknown circumstances, Caccia rose to prominence through his exceptional diplomatic skills, negotiating crucial agreements between European powers. He was appointed Archbishop of Milan in 1693, a position he held until his death in 1699. Caccia's tenure was marked by significant events, including the War of the Spanish Succession and the subsequent Treaty of Ryswick, which he played a key role in negotiating. As a leading figure in the Catholic Church, Caccia's legacy continues to shape the modern Church, with his diplomatic efforts contributing to the establishment of the modern nation-state system. His remarkable life serves as a testament to the enduring power of faith, diplomacy, and human resilience in the face of adversity. The inscription on his tombstone, 'Ego sum qui sum' ('I am who I am'), encapsulates his unwavering commitment to his faith and his unshakeable confidence in his own identity.
